Only publication of any K-TEEM wording: Schoen, Yang, Tazaz, Bray & Farina (2019), Development and Initial Field Test of the 2016 K-TEEM Test, FSU Research Report 2019-01, doi:10.33009/fsu.1581610055, ERIC ED603422 (https://files.eric.ed.gov/fulltext/ED603422.pdf) -- Appendix A, image-only, 2016 form. note: BLOCKED on instrument rights, 2026-09-08 (batch_067). No item text was written or uploaded. Quoted restrictions: Schoen Research (the K-TEEM distributor) states "These assessment resources can be made available for use in research or evaluation. Inquiries should be directed to Robert Schoen.", "Copyright 2023, Schoen Research. All rights reserved.", and that reports on "assessments with correct or incorrect answers" are "redacted to maintain security of the items so that they may remain valid for use in future studies" (https://www.schoenresearch.com/products/assessment-resources/, fetched 2026-09-08); and the only report that ever printed K-TEEM wording states "Copyright 2019, Florida State University. All rights reserved. Requests for permission to use the K-TEEM should be directed to Robert Schoen..." (ERIC ED603422, p.i). Free-but-permission-gated shape ruled on in irw#1945 (HEXACO, 2026-09-05) and the DSES ruling (2026-09-04); the rights holder's restriction overrides the source deposit's terms. INDEPENDENTLY, no source publishes wording for the 2019/2020/2021/2022 forms: the OSF deposit ships no instrument and its data-dictionary labels are boilerplate ('Dichotomously scored (correct/incorrect) variable indicating the performance of the test taker on the KCS.RPD.6 item.'), so mapping_basis=data_labels is not available; the blueprint gives only subcategory construct names; and ED603422's Appendix A is image-only and covers the superseded 2016 form. mapping_basis=unknown is recorded honestly on that basis, not guessed -- the code-to-position tie is fully documented (item = source column verbatim; blueprint Table 2 pins every code to its form position on all four forms; 0=incorrect/1=correct per the dictionary), so a reversal is a re-run rather than a restart. RETRY TEST: NO -- determinate. Would need written permission from Robert Schoen / FSU LSI, open publication of the 2019-2022 forms, or a change in the IRW ruling.
public_note: IRW does not offer item text for this instrument. The K-TEEM's rights holder reserves all rights, directs permission requests for use of the test to its author, and states that reports on its correct/incorrect items are "redacted to maintain security of the items so that they may remain valid for use in future studies" (https://www.schoenresearch.com/products/assessment-resources/). No item text was ever written or uploaded for this table.

note: Item wording from S2 File 'Measures' (DOCX) of the CC BY 4.0 PLOS ONE article 10.1371/journal.pone.0177758, 'Warmth/competence' block: a 9-item Fiske (2002) stereotype-content adjective list, 5 competence adjectives (Competent, Confident, Independent, Competitive, Intelligent) and 4 warmth adjectives (Tolerant, Warm, Sincere, Good natured). The S2 File lists the adjectives but ties them to no code, and the S3 data file's headers are bare codes (WARM1..WARM4) with no variable labels, so WARM1..WARM4 are assigned in S2 listing order (mapping_basis=paper_order) and checked against the data in verify_kraft_todd_2017_warmth.R. data/kraft_todd_2017_empathic_nonverbal.py melts the source columns unchanged, so item is the source column name. DEVIATIONS: (1) the source prints the rating scale as 0 (not at all) to 4 (very much) while both the S3 file and the live table store 1..5, so option_text is shipped shifted by one -- resp 1 = 'not at all', resp 5 = 'very much'; the direction is confirmed by all four items scoring higher under the empathic-nonverbal condition. (2) The three middle scale points are unlabelled in the source and option_text is left blank rather than padded with their own numbers. (3) The scale's sixth 'Does not apply' option is dropped as missing by the processing script and has no resp level (85/13/33/12 responses per item). (4) 'How much did the doctor seem to be______________' is the shared stem and is recorded in instructions with the rating instruction; item_text holds the adjective alone, as the source presents it.
public_note: The source questionnaire prints this scale as 0 (not at all) to 4 (very much), but the response data store it as 1-5; the shipped option labels are shifted accordingly, so resp 1 is 'not at all' and resp 5 is 'very much'. The order of 'Sincere' (WARM3) and 'Good natured' (WARM4) follows the questionnaire's listing order and could not be separated from the data.

source_ref: Kuczyk C, Munch K, Nohre M, Stephan M, de Zwaan M (2024) PLOS ONE 19(5):e0304140, doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0304140 (CC BY 4.0); S1 Data (.s006, SPSS .sav) variable labels for all 42 FBA_* items and value label set 'labels0' for the 1-5 anchors; S1 Table (.s001, TIF image) 'Pre- and post-version of the questionnaire' corroborating items 1-16 and 18-28; processing script data/kuczyk_2024_facemask.py
note: Level-1 source throughout: every one of the 42 FBA_* columns in the S1 Data .sav carries a full-sentence English variable label, and the value labels give the anchors. data/kuczyk_2024_facemask.py selects columns by prefix ([c for c in raw.columns if c.startswith('FBA')]) and melts them with var_name='item', so the IRW item code IS the source column name - no rename, no positional assignment, so Step 5b's first exemption applies and no statistical route is owed. Corroboration: S1 Table prints items 1-16 and 18-28 word for word as the labels do (including the odd past tense in pre-item 27, 'The therapist's mask made it harder for me to recognize the therapist', which the paper's own table also prints). DELIBERATE DEVIATIONS, all prefix stripping only: leading item numbering ('1. '), 'Pre 17. ' on FBA_17_pre, '29 Only pre - ' on FBA_29_in_general_pre, and 'In general pre - ' on FBA_30..42 were removed; internal wording, punctuation and the source's curly apostrophes are untouched. FBA_6's label has no terminal full stop and is shipped that way. ADMINISTERED LANGUAGE: German - inclusion required 'sufficient German language skills' and the study ran in a German psychosomatic department; no German text exists in the deposit (S1 Data holds only English labels; S1-S5 are English TIF tables), so the fallback applies and the shipped English is the authors' own rendering. ANCHORS: taken from the .sav value labels rather than the Methods section's differing English gloss ('1 = strongly disagree ... 5 = strongly agree'); both are the authors' English for the same German scale. RIGHTS: the instrument is the authors' own newly developed questionnaire, published in a CC BY 4.0 article whose supplements carry the wording; no fee, no redistribution clause and no use restriction found from any rights holder. FBA is the pre-version (27 questionnaire items, expectations, future tense) plus the two mask-preference items 17 and 29 and the 13 general public-mask validity items; the 27-item post-version is the sibling table kuczyk_2024_facemask_fbe.
public_note: Item text is the authors' own English rendering; the questionnaire was administered in German and no German wording is published in the deposit or supplements.

source_ref: Kuczyk C, Muench K, Noehre M, et al. (2024) PLOS ONE 19(5):e0304140, doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0304140 (CC BY 4.0) -- S1 Data (.s006, SPSS .sav) variable labels and value labels for all 27 FBE_* columns; S1 Table (.s001, TIF image) 'Pre- and post-version of the questionnaire', post-version block; Methods 'Item generation and study procedure' for the 5-point response scale; processing script data/kuczyk_2024_facemask.py. Cached under itemtext/.cache/kuczyk_2024_facemask_fbe/.
note: MAPPING data_labels, derivation pattern 1 (the item code IS the source column name): data/kuczyk_2024_facemask.py melts raw.columns starting with 'FBE' with var_name='item' and no rename or positional step, so FBE_9 in the live table is literally the .sav column FBE_9. All 27 live item codes matched the .sav's FBE_* columns exactly (27/27, no leftovers either way), and every one carries a variable label: e.g. FBE_9 = '9. With a mask, I could concentrate better on my issues.'. Step 5b exempt on the derivation, not on the basis. CORROBORATION: the .sav variable labels are word-for-word identical to the post-version block of S1 Table (the printed questionnaire, a TIF image read directly), 27/27, including the straight apostrophe in item 24 against curly ones elsewhere -- two independent renderings of the same English agree. DEVIATION: the leading item numbering in the labels ('1. ', '10. ') was stripped; each stripped number was asserted equal to the code's numeric suffix before stripping, so nothing was reordered. OPTIONS: the .sav value labels give 1=definitely disagree .. 5=definitely agree, identical for all 27 columns; the paper's Methods renders the same anchors as 'strongly disagree / somewhat disagree / partly agree / somewhat agree / strongly agree' -- same direction, different adverbs, and the .sav labels ship as the level-1 source. LANGUAGE: administered in German; no German text in the .sav (all labels English) or in S1-S5 or S1 Data, and the paper says the questionnaires are available on request -- so the study's own English ships in the base fields under the fallback. STEP 3B: no instrument mismatch -- FBE is the post-version (past tense, 'the mask made...'), FBA the pre-version (future tense, 'the mask will...'); the live 27 past-tense items are the experiences questionnaire the table name claims. RIGHTS: PLOS ONE article and all supplements are CC BY 4.0; the instrument is the authors' own ad hoc questionnaire developed for this study, and no fee, non-commercial or no-redistribution clause was found for it. RETRY TEST: NO -- determinate verdict, table shipped.
public_note: The questionnaire was administered in German, but neither the study's SPSS deposit nor its supplements publish the German wording (both the .sav labels and S1 Table are English and the authors state the questionnaires are available on request), so the item text shown here is the study's own English rendering rather than what respondents read; the response anchors are the .sav's value labels (1 = definitely disagree ... 5 = definitely agree), which the paper's Methods renders instead as 1 = strongly disagree ... 5 = strongly agree

source_ref: Kuehner C, Welz A, Reinhard I, Alpers GW (2017) 'Lab meets real life: A laboratory assessment of spontaneous thought and its ecological validity', PLOS ONE 12(9):e0184488, doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0184488 (CC BY 4.0) -- Methods sections 'Mind wandering (MW, AA)' and 'Perceived uncontrollability of rumination (RUM, AA)' for the item wording and the scale endpoints, and Table 1 (doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0184488.t001, image) for the per-item descriptives used in verification; response data S3 File (doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0184488.s004, SPSS .sav, no variable labels); processing script data/kuehner_2017_mw_rumination.py
note: MAPPING paper_explicit. The PLOS ONE Methods head each measure with the very code the live data uses -- 'Mind wandering (MW, AA).' and 'Perceived uncontrollability of rumination (RUM, AA).' -- and the codes are also self-describing, so this is the explicit-code-label exemption twice over. Code derivation adds nothing to check: data/kuehner_2017_mw_rumination.py melts value_vars=['MW','RUM'] from the S3 File .sav by name, so the IRW item code IS the source column name (no rename, no positional step). Checked against the data anyway, route 1: paper Table 1 publishes MW M=3.16 SD=1.90 and RUM M=1.90 SD=1.37 (both min 1, max 7), against live pooled MW 3.15/1.88 and RUM 1.90/1.37 -- largest |diff| in M = 0.010 as shipped versus 1.260 under the swapped assignment. Two items, both separated, hence VERIFIED; see verify_kuehner_2017_mw_rumination.R. TEXT transcribed verbatim from the paper's Methods, including RUM's lack of a terminal full stop as printed; nothing normalised. instructions left blank -- the paper says only that 'Participants were provided with written instructions regarding the electronic diary procedure' and never reproduces them, so nothing is invented. OPTIONS: the paper labels only MW's endpoints ('a seven-point scale ranging from 1 (I was completely on task) to 7 (I was completely off task)') and states RUM was 'rated on a scale from 1 to 7' with no anchors at all; the unlabelled points are blank. The .sav carries no value labels for MW or RUM, so there is no route-9 check to run. LANGUAGE: administered in German (Mannheim students, movisensXS); no German MW/RUM wording anywhere in the deposit -- S1 Text (s001) is the German ARSQ 2.0 only, and s002/s003/s004 have zero variable labels -- so the fallback applies, English in the base fields, _translated empty, language=German, translation_source=study_supplied (the English is the authors' own in the paper). STEP 3b: no mismatch -- 2 items on 1-7 with n=1964 each is exactly the AA MW/RUM pair, not the ARSQ dimensions (t0_* composites, fractional, not shipped) or PANAS-6 sums (6-42), both of which the processing script deliberately excluded. RIGHTS: no restriction quotable. Both probes are single items published in full in a CC BY 4.0 PLOS ONE article; MW is adapted from Killingsworth & Gilbert (2010) and RUM follows Raes et al. (2008), neither of which is a fee-licensed or no-redistribution instrument, and no rights holder's terms could be found to quote.
public_note: The two probes were administered in German to students in Mannheim, but no German wording is published in the paper or in any of its five supplementary files, so the item text shown here is the authors' own English from the paper's Methods rather than the sentences respondents read. Only the endpoints of the mind-wandering scale are labelled (1 = I was completely on task, 7 = I was completely off task); the rumination item's seven points are unlabelled in the source and are left blank

source_ref: doi:10.7910/DVN/8LBLYS (Unassisted Smoking Cessation MINIMAL ANONYMIZED DATASET.xlsx, CC0 1.0), column headers and stored response labels
note: Item text is the source spreadsheet's own column headers, which embed the code and the wording together ('(BFI_1) Is talkative'); the IRW `item` IS that full header string, so the codes are self-describing and a permutation would be self-evident. item_text is the same wording with only the '(BFI_n)' prefix stripped (the '((BFI_38)' double-paren typo is kept in `item` and stripped from item_text). option_text comes from the file's stored response labels; the label->integer map is data/kushnir2017_smoking_cessation.py's BFI_LABEL_MAP and it is VERIFIED by response-frequency matching -- all 220 item x level counts reproduce the live table exactly (e.g. BFI_1 28/67/36/113/75), with 43 of 44 items having five distinct level counts, so the 1='Disagree strongly'..5='Agree strongly' assignment is pinned rather than assumed. instructions NA: the deposit is a single data file with no preamble, and the canonical BFI-44 stem 'I see myself as someone who...' is not in the study's materials, so it was not imported. Rights: deposit is CC0 1.0; the BFI rights holder states a non-commercial restriction only ('freely available for researchers to use for non-commercial research purposes', ocf.berkeley.edu/~johnlab/bfi.html) with no fee and no redistribution clause, so under the 2026-09-04 ECR-R ruling the source deposit governs and the wording ships.
public_note: Each item's `item` value is the source file's full column header, so the join key contains the wording itself; item_text is that wording with the '(BFI_n)' prefix removed, and item BFI_38's code keeps a stray extra open parenthesis from the source. The study's materials publish no instructions, so the BFI-44 preamble and its shared stem 'I see myself as someone who...' are not included.
